description: Fixed point theory — f(x)=x, Y combinator, Banach/Brouwer/Kleene/Lawvere theorems, least/greatest fixpoints, recursive types Fix F, mu/nu types, typeability in STLC.

questions.question: What is a fixed point of a function?
questions.expected_key: f(x)=x function maps point to itself Brouwer contraction Banach
questions.gemma_answer: A value x where f(x) = x — the function maps that value to itself.

questions.question: What is the Y combinator and what does it compute?
questions.expected_key: Y=λf.(λx.f(xx))(λx.f(xx)) Y f=f(Y f) fixed point enables recursion
questions.gemma_answer: A higher-order function in lambda calculus that enables recursion by finding the fixed point of a function.

questions.question: What is Banach's fixed point theorem?
questions.expected_key: contraction mapping complete metric space unique fixed point iterate from any point converges
questions.gemma_answer: States that sequences of functions defined on a compact metric space converge to limits that are fixed points.
questions.canonical_answer: Every contraction mapping f on a non-empty complete metric space has a unique fixed point, reachable by iterating f from any starting point. A contraction satisfies d(f(x),f(y)) ≤ k·d(x,y) for k<1.

questions.question: What is Brouwer's fixed point theorem?
questions.expected_key: continuous map compact convex set to itself has fixed point disk ball topological
questions.gemma_answer: Every continuous function from a compact convex set to itself has at least one fixed point — e.g., if you stir coffee, one point ends up where it started.

questions.question: What is the difference between the least and greatest fixed points?
questions.expected_key: mu=lfp iterate from bottom inductive finite nu=gfp coinductive infinite streams
questions.gemma_answer: Least fixed point is the one closest to zero; greatest is furthest from zero in the ordering.
questions.canonical_answer: µF = least fixpoint: built by iterating F from ⊥ upward — inductive, finite, base of catamorphisms. νF = greatest fixpoint: defined coinductively from ⊤ — supports infinite structures like streams via anamorphisms.

questions.question: How does Fix F give recursive data types?
questions.expected_key: Fix F≅F(Fix F) in out morphisms F-algebra F-coalgebra list tree
questions.gemma_answer: Fix F represents the recursive type that is the fixed point of functor F — it satisfies Fix F ≅ F(Fix F).

questions.question: How does Kleene's fixed point theorem build the least fixed point?
questions.expected_key: Scott-continuous CPO bottom iterate f^n(⊥) chain supremum denotational semantics
questions.gemma_answer: Iterates the function from a bottom element on a partially ordered set, building up through the chain to the least fixed point.
questions.canonical_answer: For Scott-continuous f on a CPO with ⊥: µf = ⊔{f^n(⊥) | n≥0} — the sup of iterating f from bottom. Used in denotational semantics to give meaning to recursive programs.

questions.question: What is Lawvere's fixed point theorem?
questions.expected_key: cartesian closed category surjective transpose every endomorphism has fixed point diagonal Cantor Gödel halting
questions.gemma_answer: In category theory, if there is a surjective map from a set to its own function space, every self-map has a fixed point.
questions.canonical_answer: In a CCC, if ε:A×A→Y has a point-surjective transpose then every f:Y→Y has a fixed point. Unifies Cantor's theorem, Gödel's incompleteness, and undecidability of halting — all diagonal arguments.

questions.question: Is the Y combinator typeable in the simply typed lambda calculus?
questions.expected_key: NO requires T=T→T impossible STLC strongly normalising no general recursion
questions.gemma_answer: No, because the Y combinator requires a type that is equal to its own function type, which STLC forbids.
questions.canonical_answer: No — λx.f(x x) requires x:τ and x:τ→σ simultaneously, which is impossible in STLC. This is why STLC is strongly normalising: every program terminates. General recursion requires recursive types or untyped λ-calculus.

questions.question: How do morphisms in a category relate to fixed points of endofunctors?
questions.expected_key: Fix F initial algebra cata unique morphism from Fix F terminal coalgebra ana unique morphism to Fix F
questions.gemma_answer: Fixed points of endofunctors give the carriers of initial algebras and terminal coalgebras; morphisms out/into them are the unique fold/unfold maps.

questions.question: How can the Y combinator be used to construct recursive data types within the fixed point framework?
What role do least and greatest fixed points play in the analysis of recursive functions?
Can Banach's fixed point theorem be applied to prove the existence of solutions in certain fixed point constructions?
How does the Kleene's fixed point theorem contribute to the development of recursive type theory?

jokes.pattern: WHY DID THE FIXED POINT REFUSE TO MOVE
jokes.gemma_punchline: Because by definition it always maps to itself.
jokes.canonical_punchline: Because it was already exactly where the function needed it to be. Moving would make it a non-fixed point — and then it would cease to exist as the thing it was.

jokes.pattern: WHAT DID F OF X SAY WHEN X EQUALLED F OF X
jokes.gemma_punchline: I found my match — no more searching.
jokes.canonical_punchline: f(x) said: I am perfectly happy. x replied: that is literally the definition of me. They stayed there forever — a fixed point of the conversation.

jokes.pattern: WHY IS THE Y COMBINATOR BAD AT THERAPY
jokes.gemma_punchline: It keeps applying itself recursively to every problem without finding resolution.
jokes.canonical_punchline: It keeps applying itself recursively without reaching a base case. The therapist asked: how does that make you feel? The Y combinator said: how does that make you feel? how does that make you feel? how does—

jokes.pattern: WHAT DID BROUWER SAY TO THE FUNCTION WITH NO FIXED POINT
jokes.gemma_punchline: You are topologically impossible on a compact convex domain.
jokes.canonical_punchline: You cannot exist. If you are continuous and you map this compact convex set to itself, you must fix at least one point. The function argued it was a counterexample. Brouwer said: then you are not continuous. The function had to admit it had a hole.

jokes.pattern: WHY DOES THE FIXED POINT THEORY REFUSE TO MOVE WHEN FACED WITH ITS OWN DEFINITIO
jokes.punchline: Because it’s stuck in a loop tighter than a Banach set in a Banach space.

jokes.pattern: WHEN THE Y COMBINATOR MEETS A FUNCTION THAT DOESN’T EQUAL ITSELF, WHAT DOES IT S
jokes.punchline: It whispers, “I’m not a loop, I’m a paradox wrapped in a function.”

jokes.pattern: IN THE REALM OF LEAST AND GREATEST FIXPOINTS, WHAT HAPPENS WHEN YOU ASK A TYPE A
jokes.punchline: It gets confused, like a Kleene’s theorem trying to parse a mu-notation.

jokes.pattern: WHY DID THE RECURSIVE TYPE GET NERVOUS WHEN IT ENCOUNTERED A MU-TYPE
jokes.punchline: Because it realized it was being type-checked by the Lawvere theorem—don’t you want to be type-safe?
